players.product: network-on-chip (NoC) interconnect IP for AI SoCs

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 results, above the top end of guidance on revenue and ACV plus royalties: total revenue $24.1 million, up 46% year over year (a record); ACV plus royalties $99.5 million at quarter end, up 44% (a record); trailing 12-month royalties $8.6 million, 65% higher year over year (a record). Non-GAAP gross margin 87% (GAAP 85%, now including subcontractor costs on certain security government contracts); non-GAAP operating expense $25.5 million, lifted by $1.7 million of French employer payroll taxes on RSU vesting and higher commissions; non-GAAP operating loss $4.6 million; GAAP net loss $14.1 million. Free cash flow $8.6 million in the quarter (trailing 12 months positive $6.8 million); $123 million cash and investments, no financial debt. CEO: no single customer exceeded 10% of revenue in the first half of 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $24.1 million (+46% YoY); ACV plus royalties $99.5 million (+44%); TTM royalties $8.6 million (+65%); non-GAAP gross margin 87%; non-GAAP operating loss $4.6 million

quarterly_data.signal: Remaining performance obligation (contracted future revenue) reached $135 million at the end of Q2, an all-time high; CFO expects just over half of it to be recognized as revenue in the period starting July 1, 2026. License deal flow was driven by several large deals with existing and new customers across enterprise computing, automotive, aerospace and defense, communications, consumer and industrial, for chiplets, SoCs, ASICs, FPGAs and microcontrollers; multiple seven-figure FlexGen deals closed with major semiconductor customers in the first half.
quarterly_data.figure: RPO $135 million (record); just over half expected to be recognized starting July 1, 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance. Q3 2026: ACV plus royalties $99 million to $103 million, revenue $24 million to $25 million, non-GAAP operating loss of $3 million to $1 million. Full year 2026 (revenue raised by $3.5 million): ACV plus royalties exiting at $102 million to $106 million; revenue $95 million to $98 million, a 37% year-over-year increase at the midpoint; non-GAAP operating loss $10 million to $7 million (includes the higher French payroll-tax run rate); non-GAAP free cash flow positive $5 million to positive $9 million, unchanged. CFO: 'continued strength in semiconductors and signs of an upward trend in the cycle', a strong start to Q3, and a non-GAAP operating profit expected for a period as early as Q4 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $24 million to $25 million; FY2026 revenue $95 million to $98 million (+$3.5 million; 37% YoY at midpoint); FY ACV plus royalties $102 million to $106 million; FCF $5 million to $9 million

quarterly_data.signal: AI data-center wins. CEO: one of the world's largest hyperscale cloud companies has chosen to adopt and standardize on Arteris infrastructure silicon system IP for next-generation data centers (the customer wants to remain confidential). Separately, a large win with one of the top U.S. semiconductor design houses building ASICs for various hyperscalers — an existing but previously small customer that chose Arteris after an extensive evaluation — uses FlexGen SmartNOC IP for data movement in chiplets and multi-die chips for high-end scale-up AI compute. Enterprise computing averaged 29% of ACV plus royalties over the past four quarters, with AI infrastructure among the biggest Q2 deals; the majority of customers' Q2 design starts supported AI or HPC, and trailing 12-month design starts were 21% higher year over year.
quarterly_data.figure: enterprise computing 29% of ACV plus royalties (four-quarter average); design starts +21% (TTM)

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Speedata: Speedata, developer of the analytics processing unit (APU), has deployed Arteris in its Callisto processor for high-bandwidth, data-center analytics. Other Q2 items: an advanced automotive chip provider selected Arteris for its next-generation SoC platforms (intelligent cockpit, ADAS), and a collaboration with iCLINK by IMEC, IMEC's service provider for high-end ASICs and silicon photonics, to deploy Arteris technology in next-generation HPC chiplets and ASICs.

Customer Li Auto: Li Auto has deployed its in-house autonomous-driving chips in the L9S SUV; multiple chips designed with Arteris are used in each vehicle and run 2.56 thousand trillion operations per second (TOPS), and initial royalty contributions have started as deliveries begin. CFO: automotive royalty streams typically ramp over the first three years and then plateau; CEO: Arteris has a strong presence with China automotive OEMs.
quarterly_data.figure: 2.56 thousand trillion operations per second per vehicle; royalty ramp over the first three years

quarterly_data.signal: Royalty outlook. CFO: royalty growth paused sequentially because one customer's logistics and supply-chain issues held back a quarter's shipments (since back on stream); trailing 12-month royalties are still up 67%, but the long-term royalty CAGR guide stays at high thirties to low forties percent. CFO also cites 'very interesting strength' in deal flow from memory players (ultimately data-center related) and a $2.2 million GAAP operating-expense charge from a higher expected Cicuity earn-out; government work carries a much lower gross margin.
quarterly_data.figure: TTM royalties +67%; long-term royalty CAGR high thirties to low forties percent; $2.2 million earn-out charge

quarterly_data.signal: CEO views: data center has taken the lead in deal flow, but 'AI is going to be everywhere' and whatever happens with data-center investment 'is not going to have a major effect on us'; strong activity also in microcontrollers, automotive, embedded FPGA and space. Design cycles are fastest for data-center workload accelerators, physical AI (robotics) sits in the middle, and automotive is among the longest; functional safety plus cybersecurity assurance positions Arteris for physical AI.

connects_to.relationship: Cicuity hardware security assurance technology used in Arm CPU design

contracts.signal: Following the acquisition of Cicuity earlier in 2026, Arteris announced an expanded partnership with Arm: the hardware security assurance technology is already in use by Arm during the design phase of selected CPUs, and Arm engineering teams are expanding its adoption across additional next-generation processors. CEO: a greenfield opportunity; Cicuity is so far a non-royalty-bearing, software EDA-type model.
